Hi Alice — looping in my responses inline. Short version up front: we can support US-only residency, customer-controlled replication, PII redaction in logs, and a cold-warm failover pattern with snapshot-based cache warm-up. Details below.

1) Backups & replication
- Default: backups are stored in the same region as the primary deployment. We do not replicate backups to a different region unless cross-region replication is explicitly enabled in the deployment config.
- Opt-out: customers can disable automated cross-region replication for both persistent model checkpoints and data backups. We'll include an explicit flag in the deployment spec and the MAP.
- Encryption: backups are encrypted at-rest with customer-managed KMS keys (we support AWS KMS & HSM integrations). Keys can be region-scoped.

2) Logs & PII handling
- Default logging: request metadata (timestamp, model id, request id, latency) and high-level request/response sizes are kept for 90 days. Full request/response bodies are not retained by default for hosted sandbox deployments. For production, we retain request/response bodies for 30 days unless configured otherwise.
- PII redaction: we provide a pre-ingest redaction hook (configurable) that removes or masks fields matching regex rules or a supplied JSON schema. This hook can be enabled to redact before anything is written to our audit logs or object storage.
- Retention controls: retention windows are configurable per-customer and per-route. We can implement auto-delete policies (30/90/365 days) and provide proofs in the audit log.

3) Cross-region failover & caches
- We do not replicate live KV cache state across regions for primary-serving workloads.
- Cold-warm failover: we snapshot model state and caches to encrypted snapshots in the primary region and replicate the snapshots to the secondary (only if replication is enabled). In a failover, we restore snapshots in the secondary region (RTO depends on model size and restore throughput; typical RTO for standard LLM configs is 6–18 minutes for a warm restore; we can pressure-test for your profile).
- For ultra-low RTO we can discuss a hot-standby approach in dedicated deployments (continuous replication) but that incurs cross-region costs and has to be agreed in the contract.

4) Data categories (PHI/PII)
- We recommend classifying sensitive fields up-front and enabling the redaction hook. For embeddings and derived artifacts: customers can opt to disable storage of embeddings (use ephemeral-only inference) or request that embeddings be kept for a limited window.

5) Evidence & SOW language
- I'll attach a short blurb for procurement on KMS/HSM, backup encryption, and the region-pin option.

I'll attach a technical one-pager and a sample deployment YAML for a US-only, replication-disabled config. Let me know if you want a short (20–30 min) follow-up with infra engineers to run through restore timing and test snapshots.
